transcript:
Meeting: Harrington LLC — adapter/broker integration evaluation
Date: 2027-05-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Elena (CS), Dana (CTO Harrington), Ben (ML Eng), Priya (Infra), Marco (Product), Leah (Security)

Summary: quick discovery focused on how Harrington would integrate Redwood behind a broker/adapter pattern. Discussed SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy placement (edge vs in-cluster), per-tenant quotas and burst caps, observability hooks, and security controls (KMS, SSO, audit logs). Customer is leaning toward a private deployment for regulated workloads but wants to validate hosted/Dedicated economics and latency.

Topics: integration patterns, SDK support (py/js), LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway placement, rate limiting/quotas, observability/tracing, KMS/bring-your-own-key, SOC2/attestation, POC next steps

Action Items (as captured in call): Samir to share security pack, Ravi to drop LangChain adapter example, Priya to give QPS/token numbers, Leah to send compliance checklist.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Samir: ok everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the Harrington account. quick round-robin?
[00:07] Dana: Dana here, CTO. we build a legal-research assistant, lots of PII in documents, so security and residency matter.
[00:15] Ben: Ben, ML. we're exploring options — can't exceed 150ms 95p for search snippet generation ideally, but more importantly costs per 10k queries.
[00:23] Priya: Priya, infra. we're responsible for network and infra compliance. curious about VPC and on-prem options.
[00:29] Ravi: ravi, solutions eng. i'll cover integration patterns and latency tradeoffs.
[00:33] Marco: marco, product — interested in LangChain workflows and how much work for our engineers.
[00:38] Leah: leah, security — i'll lead compliance questions.
[00:42] Samir: great. quick context: Harrington's primary traffic is 2k qps at peak across many tenants, but most requests are small (avg 120 tokens request, 60 tokens response) — is that still accurate, Priya?
[00:53] Priya: yes approximate. we also have burst windows up to 5k qps for short intervals.
[00:58] Samir: ok that's helpful. one major decision is hosted vs dedicated vs private. can you talk constraints? regulatory or contractual obligations pushing you private?
[01:08] Dana: we have a few enterprise contracts that require customer data to remain in our VPC and a KMS we control. also some EU data residency requirements. so private or VPC-hosted control plane sounds likely. but we want to see economics of Redwood hosted for less sensitive tenants.
[01:23] Leah: also SOC2 report and audit log retention are required. do you support long-term audit export?
[01:29] Samir: yes, we have audit log exports, S3 retention, and you can enable longer retention on dedicated/private. SOC2 is available — i'll send the pack.
[01:35] Ben: technical: for our pipeline we use LangChain for orchestration and have a LlamaIndex vector store layer. How plug-and-play is Redwood's SDK and does it have icons for those libs?
[01:45] Ravi: we have a Python SDK and node SDK, and open-source LangChain + LlamaIndex adapters maintained by Redwood — they wrap client-side caching/batching and stream responses. they are drop-in in many cases, but there are config knobs for batching, kv-cache settings and streaming. we'll share a sample repo.
[01:59] Marco: if we run an adapter/broker in our cluster (edge proxy) that routes to Redwood hosted and falls back to Dedicated/private, how does auth work? we want the broker to handle multi-tenant routing.
[02:10] Ravi: typical pattern: your broker authenticates clients (SSO / your API keys), enriches headers with tenant-id, then calls Redwood with a single service account key or per-tenant keys depending on model. you can do per-tenant RBAC via Redwood's API tokens or proxy the calls through your gateway. we support short-lived tokens and fine-grained per-route policies.
[02:28] Priya: latency wise, if we run broker in region X and Redwood hosted instance in same cloud region, what's expected overhead — especially for streaming?
[02:36] Ravi: overhead usually 10-20ms network RTT if colocated; end-to-end depends on model. streaming uses chunked responses, so the broker must support HTTP/2 or chunked transfer. we can do bench numbers — ravi to send simple load script.
[02:50] Ben: we also do heavy caching at prefix level — is the KV cache accessible to the client side or is it server-side? we want to ensure caching semantics don't leak PII between tenants.
[03:00] Ravi: Redwood supports both client-side prefix caching and server-side KV caching scoped per model and per-tenant. in private deployments you can enforce tenant isolation; hosted has strict multitenant isolation and per-tenant namespaces. we'll document the exact guarantees.
[03:12] Leah: encryption — do you allow BYOK (bring your own key) with HSM/KMS? and how are keys rotated and audited?
[03:19] Samir: yes BYOK supported on Private and Dedicated. keys are rotated via your KMS and audit logs are available in the control plane. i'll include KMS integration notes in the security pack.
[03:28] Marco: what's the expected dev work to swap our existing LangChain llm wrappers to Redwood? we have a custom LlamaIndex wrapper that handles reranking.
[03:36] Ravi: in many cases it's a thin adapter — map your input to Redwood calls via SDK. LlamaIndex connector is a small shim. if you need low-latency rerank you may want to run a small rerank model in Dedicated or even on-prem and call Redwood for generation. we can share code examples.
[03:49] Ben: question on token accounting — our billing model needs per-tenant token-level visibility for chargeback. does Redwood provide token-level attribution?
[03:58] Samir: yes, per-token breakdown per API key/tenant, with logs in the console and exportable usage logs. You can compute chargeback.
[04:06] Ben: and rate limiting — can you do hierarchical quotas (global, tenant, route)? we need per-tenant rate caps and per-route burst buckets.
[04:14] Ravi: yes you can configure rate limits at account, project, and route level. Burst capacity is configurable in Dedicated with reserved capacity and burst pool for spikes. Hosted supports burst within shared limits; Dedicated gives predictable SLA.
[04:27] Priya: curious about failed fallbacks — if Dedicated is down, do you have automatic fallback to hosted? we need graceful degradation.
[04:36] Samir: we support routing policies; you can set automatic fallback to compatible model variants in other regions or hosted. there are knobes for data residency — some fallbacks might be disabled for regulated tenants.
[04:48] Leah: audit depth — can we get raw transcripts and system metadata for audits? is PII redaction supported?
[04:57] Ravi: transcripts and request logs are available in the console, you can export them. PII redaction tooling is offered as an addon or you can run pre-processing in your broker to strip/transform content before sending.
[05:07] Marco: ok timeline: we have procurement windows next quarter. we'd like to run a short POC to validate latency and cost for one tenant group. what's a realistic pilot?
[05:16] Samir: common pilot: 2-week POC with Dedicated trial or private dev environment. we can provide trial credits and a sandbox account; SE-led benchmarking. Ravi will help with bench scripts.
[05:25] Ben: for the POC we want to simulate 1k qps at 95p of 150 ms for small prompts. can Redwood Dedicated hit that on a 4-GPU pool?
[05:33] Ravi: depends on model and batching. with optimized kernels and correct batching you can hit those numbers for smaller models; i'll scope recommended instance type after seeing your token distribution.
[05:44] Priya: networking — will we need special peering? for private deployment, how does control plane connect?
[05:51] Samir: Private offers VPC peering and private link options; on-prem has an air-gapped package if needed. control plane can be customer-managed if you want total control.
[06:02] Leah: compliance: do you provide pen test reports or only SOC2?
[06:07] Samir: SOC2, ISO summary, and for enterprise we provide pen test summaries under NDA.
[06:12] Dana: are there any gotchas with LangChain/LLamaIndex adapters — like loss of streaming, or missing function-calling features?
[06:20] Ravi: function-calling semantics are supported; streaming is supported for python/node SDKs. some adapters may buffer for chunked outputs; we'll show patterns for streaming through LangChain.
[06:31] Marco: how about observability hooks? our SREs want distributed tracing and per-request tags for our own APM.
[06:38] Ravi: we emit trace headers, support open-telemetry integration, and have per-request metadata you can ingest. console also gives per-route latency, token breakdown and tail-latency histograms.
[06:49] Ben: competitor question — some firms just self-host llama with a sidecar cache to save cost. why would we pick Redwood?
[06:57] Samir: tradeoffs: self-host gives control but costs engineering time and ops; Redwood provides optimized runtime, model tuning, observability and unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private which reduces total cost. we also help with model quantization guidance and kernel-level perf.
[07:12] Leah: security question again — if we run broker in our cluster and logs go to Redwood for observation, what's the SLA on log delivery and retention?
[07:21] Samir: default retention is 90 days on hosted; dedicated/private can be configured to longer retention or export to your S3. SLA on logging depends on plan; i'll include specifics in the pack.
[07:31] Priya: onboarding friction: how long to get a private deployment up for initial pilot?
[07:36] Ravi: for a private dev environment typically 2-4 weeks with our infra team; Dedicated can often start faster. depends on network approvals and KMS setup.
[07:46] Marco: any limits on model uploads or custom models on dedicated/private?
[07:51] Samir: you can bring custom models in private and dedicated with some model onboarding work; we help with compatibility checks and quantization recommendations.
[07:59] Ben: what about per-tenant model pinning for A/B tests? we'd like to route some tenants to a different model version.
[08:07] Ravi: supported — route-based model pinning and canary rollouts. console supports experiments and rollback.
[08:14] Leah: one more — encryption at rest for logs and snapshots?
[08:18] Samir: yes, SSE with KMS, and for private we can integrate with your HSM.
[08:23] Marco: ok next steps recap?
[08:26] Samir: recap: Samir send security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, KMS notes). Ravi send LangChain adapter example and simple bench script. Priya to provide qps/token spreadsheet and Leah to send compliance Qs. We'll schedule POC scoping with infra + security next week.
[08:42] Dana: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:46] Samir: thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invite for POC scoping.

End of transcript.
